subject: DSM with 'presence' as the response (family = binomial)

messages.author: 3314d7ad28eab19e
messages.subject: DSM with 'presence' as the response (family = binomial)
parts:
Dear group,

I'm fitting DSMs to point survey data using 'dsm' in R and have become curious about how this model works when the response is changed to 'presence.' Specifically, the response variable is 0 when birds are not detected and 1 when at least 1 individual is detected. In this sense, the data are being treated as presence/absence, but I cannot work out how this model makes adjustments for detection probability. I'm also unable to find literature describing this particular version of the DSM beyond what is listed in the R package vignette.

As an example, my model call is the following, assuming a distance-detection function has already been fit using a hazard rate function:

dsm.pres.1 = dsm( presence ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + s(time), ddf.obj = hr.model, segment.data = seg.data, observation.data=obs.data, weights=1, group=TRUE, family=binomial()) 

I can reclassify the presence/absence response into 0s & 1s and fit those using gam with family=binomial. However, I get much different coefficient estimates for the effects of x1, x2, x3, and s(time). What is dsm doing here that gam is not doing? More specifically, I notice that even though I have set weights=1, there is an attribute of the fitted model object called 'weights' and also 'working.weights' which are the same vector of weights, distributed between 0 and 0.25 and same length as my data. I can access these via 'dsm.pres.1$weights.'
       
So my questions are, A) what are these weights and how are they being generated, and B) are they responsible for the difference between the dsm and gam being fit to the same binary response variable with same predictors?

Thanks for considering my question.
best,
Shawn

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM with 'presence' as the response (family = binomial)
parts:
Hi Shawn, hi listfolks,

The presence response was added for convenience to look at issues with
problem datasets (some years ago!) so data could be formatted easily. It
was not intended for any serious modelling. Detectability is ignored.
This was not obvious in the documentation and wrong in some cases in the
code, so I've made some changes and pushed these to the github version
of the package. I still don't recommend using this option though, better
to use a package that's actually set up for this kind of modelling.

Regarding weights, note that the $weights in the returned object are the
iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) weights from the gam fitting
procedure NOT the "prior" weights given to gam() or dsm(). See
?gamObject/?gam.


Hope this helps,
--dave
